message.reasoning:
We need to generate high-quality unit test code for the focal method isLessThan(Number) of NumericIndicator, using JUnit5 and Mockito. We already have a test class framework with several tests. Need to incorporate all test cases from JSON, covering standard cases, boundary cases, negative, floating point, null, BigDecimal, large values, NaN, infinities, BigInteger, etc., plus exception scenarios. Also need to test exception when NumericIndicator constructed with null delegate. Also test custom Number that throws exception.

We should keep existing tests and add parameterized tests for many cases. Use @ParameterizedTest with @MethodSource. For each case, we need to evaluate rule.isSatisfied(index) for each index and compare expected behavior. Could generate expected boolean array? But expected description is generic. We can implement a test that iterates series and asserts rule.isSatisfied(i) matches condition (value < n). Use series values we have: 1..9 then 8..1,0,-1,-2. So we can compute expected by comparing each series close price (Num) to given Number using Num.compareTo(Num). Need to convert Number to Num via DecimalNum.valueOf. Use rule = numericIndicator.isLessThan(n). Then for each index, compute expected = closePriceIndicator.getValue(i).isLessThan(DecimalNum.valueOf(n)). However need to handle NaN, infinities, etc. DecimalNum may not support NaN? It may treat Double.NaN as NaN. We'll just use Num's isLessThan? Or compare using doubleValue. Simpler: compute double value = series.getBar(i).getClosePrice().doubleValue()? Not accessible maybe. Use closePriceIndicator.getValue(i).doubleValue(). Then compare using Java double semantics: if n is Double.NaN, any comparison returns false. For infinities, double comparisons work.

We'll need to handle Number null: expect NullPointerException.

For delegate null case: create NumericIndicator via NumericIndicator.of(null) -> likely NPE later. We'll test that calling isLessThan throws NPE.

For custom FaultyNumber that throws in doubleValue: define inner class FaultyNumber extends Number with methods throwing. Expect RuntimeException.

We'll add parameterized tests for many numeric types.

We must not modify @Before/@After.

We'll add new test methods after existing ones.

Implementation steps:

- Keep existing test class content.
- Add import for ParameterizedTest, MethodSource, etc.
- Add static Stream<Arguments> provideNumbers() returning arguments: Number n, String description maybe. Use cases from JSON except null and exception scenarios. We'll include: Integer 10, Integer 0, Integer -5, Double 3.14159, BigDecimal 100, Long.MAX_VALUE, Double.MIN_VALUE, Float 5.5f, Short 2, Byte -1, Double.NaN, Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY, Double.NEGATIVE_INFINITY, BigInteger 12345678901234567890, Double 0.0.

- For each, test that rule is UnderIndicatorRule and that rule.isSatisfied(i) matches expected condition: value < n (strict). For NaN, rule.isSatisfied always false. For POSITIVE_INFINITY, all finite values true (including negative). For NEGATIVE_INFINITY, always false.

- Use helper method computeExpected(Num value, Number n) that returns boolean.

- For null Number case: separate test expecting NullPointerException.

- For delegate null: test that constructing numericIndicator = NumericIndicator.of(null) and calling isLessThan throws NPE.

- For FaultyNumber: define class FaultyNumber extends Number with doubleValue throwing new RuntimeException("faulty"). Implement other methods returning 0 maybe. Expect RuntimeException.

Add comments.

Make sure imports: org.junit.jupiter.params.ParameterizedTest, org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.MethodSource, org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.Arguments, java.util.stream.Stream, java.math.BigDecimal, java.math.BigInteger.

Now produce final code block.
